title: Fine-Grained Selector Store (Zustand / Redux pattern)
problemStatement: Implement `createStore(initialState)` with methods: `getState()`, `setState(partial)`, and `useSelector(selector, equalityFn = Object.is)`. Subscribers are only notified when their selected slice of state actually changes.
interviewTrap: Global state stores that notify all components regardless of which slice changed cause massive app-wide re-render cascades.

testCases.name: Notifies selector subscriber only when selected property changes
testCases.testFn: const store = createStore({ count: 0, text: 'hi' }); const notifications = []; store.subscribeSelector(s => s.count, val => notifications.push(val)); store.setState({ count: 10 }); return notifications;

testCases.name: Does not notify subscriber when unrelated state changes
testCases.input: updating text does not notify counter subscriber
testCases.testFn: const store = createStore({ count: 0, text: 'hi' }); let calls = 0; store.subscribeSelector(s => s.count, () => calls++); store.setState({ text: 'updated' }); return calls;

testCases.name: Unsubscribe cleans up listener properly
testCases.testFn: const store = createStore({ count: 0 }); let calls = 0; const unsub = store.subscribeSelector(s => s.count, () => calls++); store.setState({ count: 1 }); unsub(); store.setState({ count: 2 }); return calls;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: By default, when a parent component renders, all its child components re-render recursively regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` bails out only if all props are shallowly equal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Selective Re-renders & Subscription Notification.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Selective Re-renders & Subscription Notification is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Global state stores that notify all components regardless of which slice changed cause massive app-wide re-render cascades.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do selector stores (Zustand / Redux) prevent unnecessary re-renders compared to React Context?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: React Context triggers re-renders on ALL consuming components whenever the context value reference changes, even if a component only consumes a small property. Selector stores use external subscriptions outside of React (`useSyncExternalStore`): components pass a selector `state => state.user.name`. The store checks if the selector output changed via `Object.is`; if not, the component skips re-rendering entirely.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does useSyncExternalStore prevent 'Tearing' in Concurrent React?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 'Tearing' occurs in Concurrent Mode when a component starts rendering with state version 1, yields to the browser, an external store mutates to version 2, and a sibling component renders version 2, resulting in an inconsistent UI. `useSyncExternalStore` detects external store mutations during render and forces a synchronous fallback to guarantee consistent UI snapshots.

realWorldUseCases.description: Subscribing to fine-grained state slices in enterprise apps without context re-render cascades.

howToExplain.opening: Fine-grained selector stores bypass React Context re-render cascades by maintaining external subscriptions and notifying only components whose selected slice has changed.
keyPoints: Context re-renders all consumers on any value change.
Selector stores evaluate slice equality (Object.is) before scheduling component renders.
useSyncExternalStore integrates external stores safely with Concurrent React.
Achieves O(1) targeted renders in massive state trees.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Fine-grained subscriptions scale state management to hundreds of thousands of updates without performance degradation.
analogies: A news subscription: instead of receiving the entire 500-page Sunday paper when you only care about sports, you receive a text message alert only when your favorite team scores.

commonMistakes.mistake: Returning a new object literal in a selector without equality comparison: state => ({ a: state.a, b: state.b }).
commonMistakes.why: Returning a new object reference on every state change causes the selector to fail equality checks, forcing re-renders on every action.
commonMistakes.correct: Use shallow equality or split into multiple separate selector hooks.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is the three-argument signature of useSyncExternalStore?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot)`. `subscribe` registers listeners, `getSnapshot` returns the current client state, and `getServerSnapshot` returns initial SSR state for hydration consistency.
